title: `ResourceEditPage` discards the kernel's `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` sentence, so the operator-facing hatch clause never reaches a Studio author
body:
Observation found while implementing objectstack-ai/objectstack#8361 (PR objectstack-ai/objectstack#8630). Filed, not fixed, and **deliberately framed as an observation rather than a defect** — the substitution below is very likely the intended remedy pattern from framework#7307 / framework#7414, both closed.

## What was measured

`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ResourceEditPage.tsx:1160` maps the kernel's refusal to a fixed localized string:

```ts
else if (errorCodeIs(err, 'WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED')) {
  setError(t('engine.package.writableRequired', locale));
}
```

`engine.package.writableRequired` is a constant: *"Pick or create a writable base (package) first — this item cannot be authored into a read-only code package."* The backend's own sentence is dropped entirely.

## Why it is worth recording now

framework#8361 just made the ADR-0070 D1 refusal carry a **conditional** clause — emitted only when `OS_METADATA_WRITABLE` is set for the type:

> (OS_METADATA_WRITABLE is set for 'permission': it unlocks the metadata TYPE, not package writability, so it does not make a read-only package a writable base.)

That clause exists for exactly one reader: an operator who has just set the variable and needs to know it does not reach the package dimension. It now reaches API, CLI and AI-tool callers. On this Studio surface it is discarded before rendering, because the mapping is keyed on the error **code** and the code is identical in both cases — the two refusals are indistinguishable to this branch by construction.

Nothing regressed here: the clause never reached this surface, and the localized string is not wrong. The gap is that the conditional half of the diagnostic has no channel to a Studio author at all.

## Not proposing a shape

Three directions, none obvious enough to act on unasked, and the first is a real ruling question rather than a code question:

1. Leave it — Studio authors are not the audience for an env-var hatch diagnostic, and framework#7307 / framework#7414 closed on the principle that raw backend sentences do not belong in front of end users. This may simply be correct.
2. A second i18n key selected on a structured hint from the error envelope (the framework would need to carry the hatch fact as a **field**, not as prose — the code and status are identical in both cases today).
3. Append the backend sentence as secondary detail under the localized headline, which reopens exactly what framework#7307 closed.

Option 2 is the only one that does not re-litigate a settled ruling, but it needs a framework-side envelope field that does not exist, so it is a cross-repo design call rather than a UI change.

## Related

- objectstack-ai/objectstack#8361 / PR objectstack-ai/objectstack#8630 — where the clause became reachable
- objectstack-ai/objectstack#8146 — where the `hatchOpen` remedy selection landed
- objectstack-ai/objectstack#7307, objectstack-ai/objectstack#7414 — the closed cards that established "do not show the raw backend sentence to end users"
